verses.1:1: Love righteousness, you who judge the earth; think about the Lord in goodness, and in simplicity of heart seek Him.
verses.1:2: For He is found by those who do not test Him, and He manifests Himself to those who do not distrust Him.
verses.1:3: For crooked reasonings separate one from God, and His power, when tested, convicts the foolish.
verses.1:4: For wisdom will not enter into a soul that devises evil, nor will it dwell in a body indebted to sin.
verses.1:5: For the holy spirit of discipline will flee from deceit, and will depart from senseless reasonings, and will be put to shame when unrighteousness approaches.
verses.1:6: For wisdom is a spirit that loves humanity, yet it will not hold a blasphemer guiltless for his lips; because God is a witness of his inward parts, and a true overseer of his heart, and a hearer of his tongue.
verses.1:7: For the Spirit of the Lord has filled the inhabited world, and that which holds all things together has knowledge of speech.
verses.1:8: Because of this, no one who utters unrighteous things will escape notice, nor indeed will justice, when it convicts, pass him by.
verses.1:9: For there will be an examination into the counsels of an ungodly person, and the report of his words will come to the Lord for the conviction of his lawless deeds.
verses.1:10: Because an ear of jealousy listens to all things, and the sound of grumblings is not hidden.
verses.1:11: Guard yourselves, therefore, against useless grumbling, and spare your tongue from slander; for a secret utterance will not go empty, and a lying mouth destroys a soul.
verses.1:12: Do not eagerly desire death in the error of your life, nor draw destruction upon yourselves by the works of your hands;
verses.1:13: for God did not make death, nor does He delight in the ruin of the living.
verses.1:14: For He created all things so that they might exist, and the creatures of the world are wholesome, and there is no poison of destruction in them, nor is there a kingdom of Hades on earth.
verses.1:16: But the ungodly summoned him with their hands and with their words; considering him a friend, they pined away, and they made a covenant with him, because they are worthy to belong to his portion.
verses.2:1: For they said among themselves, not reasoning rightly, "Our life is short and sorrowful, and there is no remedy at a person's end, and no one has been known to return from Hades.
verses.2:2: For we came into being by chance, and after this we will be as though we had not existed; for the breath in our nostrils is smoke, and reason is a spark in the movement of our heart,
verses.2:3: and when it is extinguished, the body will turn into ashes, and the spirit will be dispersed like thin air.
verses.2:4: And our name will be forgotten in time, and no one will remember our works; and our life will pass away like the traces of a cloud, and will be scattered like a mist driven away by the rays of the sun and weighed down by its heat.
verses.2:5: For our life is the passing of a shadow, and there is no reversal of our end, because it has been sealed, and no one returns.
verses.2:6: Come, therefore, and let us enjoy the good things that exist, and let us eagerly make use of creation as in youth.
verses.2:7: Let us be filled with costly wine and perfumes, and let no flower of the air pass us by;
verses.2:8: let us crown ourselves with rosebuds before they wither.
verses.2:9: Let none of us be without a share in our revelry; everywhere let us leave tokens of gladness, for this is our portion, and this is our lot.
verses.2:10: Let us oppress a righteous poor man; let us not spare a widow, nor respect the aged gray hairs of an old man.
verses.2:11: But let our strength be the law of righteousness, for what is weak is proved useless.
verses.2:12: And let us lie in wait for the righteous man, because he is inconvenient to us and opposes our works, and reproaches us for sins against the law, and charges us with sins against our discipline.
verses.2:13: He professes to have knowledge of God, and calls himself a child of the Lord.
verses.2:14: He has become to us a reproof of our thoughts;
verses.2:15: he is burdensome to us even to look at, because his life is unlike that of others, and his paths are strange.
verses.2:16: We have been considered counterfeit by him, and he keeps away from our ways as from impurities; he calls the final end of the righteous blessed, and boasts of God as his father.
verses.2:17: Let us see whether his words are true, and let us test what happens at his departure.
verses.2:18: For if the righteous man is a son of God, He will help him and rescue him from the hand of those who oppose him.
verses.2:19: With insult and torment let us examine him, so that we may know his gentleness and judge his patient endurance.
verses.2:20: Let us condemn him to a shameful death, for according to his words, there will be a visitation for him."
verses.2:21: These things they reasoned, and they were led astray; for their wickedness blinded them, and they did not know the mysteries
verses.2:22: of Him, nor did they hope for a reward of holiness, nor did they discern a prize for blameless souls.
verses.2:23: For God created man for incorruption, and made him an image of His own nature;
verses.2:24: but by the envy of the devil, death entered into the world, and those who belong to his portion experience it.
verses.3:1: But the souls of the righteous are in God's hand, and torment will by no means touch them.
verses.3:2: In the eyes of the foolish they appeared to have died,
verses.3:3: and their departure was considered affliction, and their journey away from us ruin; but they are in peace.
verses.3:4: For even if they are punished in the sight of people, their hope is full of immortality.
verses.3:5: And having been disciplined a little, they will receive great good, because God tested them and found them worthy of Himself.
verses.3:6: Like gold in a smelting furnace He proved them, and like a whole burnt offering of sacrifice He accepted them.
verses.3:7: And in the time of their visitation they will shine forth, and like sparks among stubble they will run about.
verses.3:8: They will judge nations and rule over peoples, and the Lord will reign over them forever.
verses.3:9: Those who have put their trust in Him will understand truth, and those who are faithful will remain with Him in love, for grace and mercy belong to His chosen ones.
verses.3:10: But the ungodly will receive punishment according to what they reasoned, those who disregarded the righteous one and turned away from the Lord.
verses.3:11: For whoever despises wisdom and discipline is wretched, and their hope is empty, and their labors are unprofitable, and their works are useless.
verses.3:12: Their wives are foolish, and their children are wicked;
verses.3:13: cursed is their offspring. For blessed is the barren woman who is undefiled, who has not known a bed in transgression; she will have fruit in the visitation of souls.
verses.3:14: And blessed is the eunuch who has done no lawless deed with his hand, nor thought evil things against the Lord; for a choice favor will be given to him for his faithfulness, and a more pleasing lot in the temple of the Lord.
verses.3:15: For the fruit of good labors is glorious, and the root of understanding is unfailing.
verses.3:16: But children of adulterers will not reach maturity, and the seed from an unlawful bed will be wiped out.
verses.3:17: For even if they become long-lived, they will be considered as nothing, and in the end their old age will be without honor.
verses.3:18: And if they die quickly, they have no hope, nor consolation in the day of decision;
verses.3:19: for the end of an unrighteous generation is harsh.
verses.4:1: Better is childlessness with virtue, for immortality is in the memory of it, because it is known both by God and by people.
verses.4:2: When it is present they imitate it, and when it has departed they long for it; and throughout eternity it marches in triumph wearing a crown, having won the contest for undefiled prizes.
verses.4:3: But the prolific multitude of the ungodly will be of no use, and from illegitimate shoots it will not send down a deep root nor establish a secure foundation.
verses.4:4: For even if they flourish in branches for a time, standing insecurely they will be shaken by wind, and by the violence of winds they will be uprooted.
verses.4:5: Immature branches will be broken off, and their fruit is useless, unripe for eating and fit for nothing.
verses.4:6: For children born from lawless unions are witnesses of wickedness against parents at their examination.
verses.4:7: But a righteous person, even if he dies early, will be at rest.
verses.4:8: For honorable old age is not that of long duration, nor is it measured by a count of years.
verses.4:9: Rather, gray hair for people is prudence, and the maturity of old age is an unblemished life.
verses.4:10: Having become pleasing to God, he was loved, and while living among sinners he was transferred.
verses.4:11: He was snatched away so that evil might not alter his understanding, or deceit delude his soul.
verses.4:12: For the fascination of baseness obscures what is good, and the roving of desire undermines an innocent mind.
verses.4:13: Having been perfected in a short time, he fulfilled long years.
verses.4:14: For his soul was pleasing to the Lord; therefore he hastened out of the midst of wickedness.
verses.4:15: But the peoples saw and did not understand, nor did they take such a thing to mind, that grace and mercy are upon His chosen ones, and watchful care is upon His devout ones.
verses.4:16: But a righteous person who has died will condemn the living ungodly, and youth quickly completed will condemn the long old age of an unrighteous person.
verses.4:17: For they will see the end of a wise person, and they will not understand what He purposed concerning him, and for what purpose the Lord kept him safe.
verses.4:18: They will see and show contempt, but the Lord will laugh at them in derision; and after this they will become a dishonored corpse and a disgrace among the dead forever.
verses.4:19: For He will dash them down speechless and headlong, and He will shake them from their foundations; and to the very last they will be laid waste, and they will be in anguish, and their memory will perish.
verses.4:20: They will come fearful at the reckoning of their sins, and their lawless deeds will convict them to their face.
verses.5:1: Then the righteous one will stand with great boldness before the face of those who afflicted him and those who disregarded his labors.
verses.5:2: At the sight they will be troubled with dreadful fear, and they will be astounded at the unexpectedness of salvation.
verses.5:3: They will say among themselves in remorse, and through distress of spirit they will groan, "This was the one whom we once held as an object of laughter and as a byword of reproach,
verses.5:4: we fools! We counted his life madness and his end without honor.
verses.5:5: How was he numbered among the sons of God, and his lot is among the holy ones?
verses.5:6: So then we strayed from the way of truth, and the light of righteousness did not shine on us, and the sun did not rise for us.
verses.5:7: We had our fill of the paths of lawlessness and destruction, and we traveled through trackless deserts, but we did not know the way of the Lord.
verses.5:8: What did arrogance profit us? And what has wealth with boasting contributed to us?
verses.5:9: All those things passed away like a shadow, and like a message hurrying by;
verses.5:10: like a ship passing through billowing water, of which, when it has gone by, no trace can be found, nor the track of its keel in the waves;
verses.5:11: or as when a bird flies through the air, no evidence of its course is found, but the light air, lashed by the stroke of pinions and split by the force of their rushing, is traversed as wings move, and after this no sign of passage is found in it;
verses.5:12: or as when an arrow is shot at a target, the parted air immediately closes back into itself, so that its path is unknown;
verses.5:13: so we also, once born, ceased to be, and we had no sign of virtue to show, but in our evil we were utterly consumed."
verses.5:14: For the hope of an ungodly person is like chaff carried by wind, and like thin frost driven by a storm, and like smoke it is dispersed by wind, and like the remembrance of a one-day guest it passes by.
verses.5:15: But the righteous live forever, and their reward is in the Lord, and care for them is with the Most High.
verses.5:16: Therefore they will receive the royal crown of splendor and the diadem of beauty from the hand of the Lord, because with His right hand He will shelter them, and with His arm He will shield them.
verses.5:17: He will take His zeal as full armor, and He will arm creation for vengeance against enemies.
verses.5:18: He will put on righteousness as a breastplate, and He will wear impartial judgment as a helmet.
verses.5:19: He will take holiness as an invincible shield,
verses.5:20: and He will sharpen relentless wrath into a sword, and the world will fight alongside Him against the senseless.
verses.5:21: Well-aimed bolts of lightning will go forth, and as from a well-curved bow of the clouds they will leap to the target,
verses.5:22: and from a catapult hailstones full of fury will be hurled; the water of the sea will rage against them, and rivers will overwhelm them relentlessly.
verses.5:23: A wind of power will stand against them, and like a storm it will winnow them away; and all lawlessness will lay waste the earth, and evildoing will overturn the thrones of rulers.
verses.6:1: Hear therefore, kings, and understand; learn, judges of the ends of the earth.
verses.6:2: Give ear, you who rule over a multitude and boast over throngs of nations.
verses.6:3: For dominion was given to you from the Lord, and sovereignty from the Most High, who will examine your works and search out your counsels,
verses.6:4: because, being servants of His kingdom, you did not judge rightly, nor keep the law, nor walk according to the counsel of God.
verses.6:5: Terribly and swiftly He will come upon you, because relentless judgment comes upon those in high places.
verses.6:6: For the lowliest may be pardoned in mercy, but the mighty will be mightily tested.
verses.6:7: For the Master of all will not shrink before any person, nor stand in awe of greatness, because He Himself made small and great, and He provides for all alike.
verses.6:8: But for the powerful, a strict inquiry awaits.
verses.6:9: To you therefore, O monarchs, are my words, so that you may learn wisdom and not fall away.
verses.6:10: For those who keep holy things in holiness will be made holy, and those who have been taught them will find a defense.
verses.6:11: Therefore desire my words; long for them, and you will be instructed.
verses.6:12: Wisdom is radiant and unfading, and she is easily seen by those who love her.
verses.6:13: She anticipates those who desire her, making herself known beforehand.
verses.6:14: The one who rises early for her will not grow weary, for he will find her sitting beside his gates.
verses.6:15: For to reflect upon her is the perfection of prudence, and the one who stays awake for her sake will quickly be free from anxiety.
verses.6:16: For she herself goes about seeking those worthy of her, and in the paths she appears graciously to them, and in every thought she meets them.
verses.6:17: For the truest beginning of her is desire for instruction, and care for instruction is love,
verses.6:18: and love is the keeping of her laws, and attention to laws is the assurance of incorruptibility,
verses.6:19: and incorruptibility causes one to be near God.
verses.6:20: Therefore desire for wisdom leads up to a kingdom.
verses.6:21: If therefore you delight in thrones and scepters, monarchs of peoples, honor wisdom, so that you may reign forever.
verses.6:22: Now I will declare what wisdom is and how she came into being, and I will not hide mysteries from you, but I will trace her out from the beginning of creation and bring the knowledge of her into the open, and I will by no means pass by the truth.
verses.6:23: Neither indeed will I travel with wasting envy, because it will have no fellowship with wisdom.
verses.6:24: But a multitude of the wise is the salvation of the world, and a prudent king is the stability of a people.
verses.6:25: Therefore be instructed by my words, and you will profit.
verses.7:1: I also am a mortal, equal to all, and a descendant of the earthborn one who was first formed.
verses.7:2: And in a mother's womb I was sculpted into flesh during a ten-month period, congealed in blood from the seed of a man and the pleasure that accompanied sleep.
verses.7:3: And when I too was born, I drew in the common air and fell upon the earth of like nature, weeping with a first cry the same as all alike.
verses.7:4: I was raised in swaddling cloths and with cares.
verses.7:5: For no king had a different beginning of birth;
verses.7:6: but there is one entrance into life for all, and an equal departure.
verses.7:7: Therefore I prayed, and understanding was given to me; I called out, and a spirit of wisdom came to me.
verses.7:8: I preferred her to scepters and thrones, and I considered wealth nothing in comparison with her.
verses.7:9: Nor did I liken a priceless stone to her, because all gold in her sight is a little sand, and silver will be counted as clay before her.
verses.7:10: I loved her more than health and beauty, and I chose to have her instead of light, because the brightness from her is sleepless.
verses.7:11: Yet all good things came to me together with her, and countless wealth in her hands.
verses.7:12: And I rejoiced over them all, because wisdom leads them, yet I did not know that she was the origin of these things.
verses.7:13: I learned without deceit, and I share ungrudgingly; I do not hide her wealth.
verses.7:14: For she is an unfailing treasure for people; those who make use of it secure friendship with God, being commended because of the gifts that come from instruction.
verses.7:15: May God grant to me to speak with judgment and to think worthily of the things that have been given, because He Himself is both the guide of wisdom and the corrector of the wise.
verses.7:16: For in His hand are both we and our words, and all understanding and knowledge of crafts.
verses.7:17: For He Himself gave to me unerring knowledge of the things that exist, to know the structure of the world and the working of the elements,
verses.7:18: the beginning and end and middle of times, the alternations of the solstices and the changes of the seasons,
verses.7:19: the cycles of the years and the positions of the stars,
verses.7:20: the natures of animals and the tempers of wild beasts, the forces of winds and the reasonings of people, the varieties of plants and the powers of roots.
verses.7:21: And all things, both hidden and manifest, I came to know.
verses.7:22: For wisdom, the artisan of all things, taught me. For in her is a spirit that is intelligent, holy, unique, manifold, subtle, mobile, clear, unstained, distinct, unharmed, loving the good, keen, unhindered, beneficent,
verses.7:23: loving humanity, steadfast, secure, free from anxiety, all-powerful, overseeing all, and penetrating through all spirits that are intelligent, pure, and most subtle.
verses.7:24: For wisdom is more mobile than any motion, and she pervades and penetrates through all things because of her purity.
verses.7:25: For she is a vapor of the power of God, and an unalloyed outflowing of the glory of the Almighty; because of this, nothing defiled slips into her.
verses.7:26: For she is a radiance of everlasting light, and an unblemished mirror of God's working, and an image of His goodness.
verses.7:27: And being one, she can do all things, and remaining in herself, she renews all things; and generation by generation passing into holy souls, she fashions friends of God and prophets.
verses.7:28: For God loves nothing except the one who dwells with wisdom.
verses.7:29: For she is more splendid than the sun, and above every arrangement of stars. Compared with light, she is found superior;
verses.7:30: for night succeeds it, but wickedness does not prevail against wisdom.
verses.8:1: And she extends strongly from end to end, and governs all things well.
verses.8:2: Her I loved and sought out from my youth, and I sought to take her as a bride for myself, and I became a lover of her beauty.
verses.8:3: She glorifies her noble birth by having companionship with God, and the Master of all loved her.
verses.8:4: For she is an initiate of the knowledge of God, and a chooser of His works.
verses.8:5: And if wealth is a desirable possession in life, what is wealthier than wisdom, who works all things?
verses.8:6: And if understanding is at work, who more than she is an artisan of the things that exist?
verses.8:7: And if anyone loves righteousness, her labors are virtues; for she teaches self-control and understanding, righteousness and courage; nothing in life is more useful to people than these.
verses.8:8: And if anyone also longs for wide experience, she knows the things of old and how to surmise the things to come; she understands turns of speech and solutions of riddles; she foreknows signs and wonders and the outcomes of seasons and times.
verses.8:9: Therefore I decided to take her for companionship, knowing that she would be a counselor of good things to me, and an encouragement in cares and grief.
verses.8:10: Because of her I will have glory among the crowds, and honor among the elders, though I am young.
verses.8:11: I will be found keen in judgment, and in the sight of rulers I will be admired.
verses.8:12: When I am silent they will wait for me, and when I speak they will pay attention; and when I talk at greater length, they will place a hand upon their mouth.
verses.8:13: Because of her I will have immortality, and I will leave behind an eternal memory to those after me.
verses.8:14: I will govern peoples, and nations will be subjected to me.
verses.8:15: Terrifying tyrants will fear me when they hear of me; among the multitude I will appear good, and in war courageous.
verses.8:16: When I enter my house, I will find rest with her; for association with her has no bitterness, nor does companionship with her have pain, but gladness and joy.
verses.8:17: Having considered these things within myself, and having pondered in my heart that there is immortality in kinship with wisdom,
verses.8:18: and in friendship with her is good delight, and in the labors of her hands is unfailing wealth, and in the exercise of her company is understanding, and renown in the fellowship of her words, I went about seeking how I might take her to myself.
verses.8:19: Now I was a gifted child, and I received a good soul as my portion;
verses.8:20: or rather, being good, I entered an undefiled body.
verses.8:21: But knowing that I would not otherwise possess her unless God gave her—and this too belonged to understanding, to know whose the gift is—I appealed to the Lord and pleaded with Him, and said from my whole heart:
verses.9:1: "God of the fathers and Lord of Your mercy, who made all things by Your word,
verses.9:2: and by Your wisdom fashioned man, so that he might have dominion over the creatures made by You,
verses.9:3: and rule the world in holiness and righteousness, and render judgment in uprightness of soul:
verses.9:4: give me wisdom, who sits beside Your throne, and do not reject me from among Your children.
verses.9:5: For I am Your servant and the son of Your maidservant, a weak and short-lived man, and deficient in comprehension of judgment and laws.
verses.9:6: For even if someone is perfect among the sons of men, if the wisdom that comes from You is absent, he will be counted as nothing.
verses.9:7: You chose me as king of Your people and judge of Your sons and daughters.
verses.9:8: You gave command to build a temple on Your holy mountain, and an altar in the city of Your dwelling, a copy of the holy tent that You prepared beforehand from the beginning.
verses.9:9: And with You is wisdom, who knows Your works and was present when You were making the world, and who understands what is pleasing in Your eyes and what is right in Your commandments.
verses.9:10: Send her forth from the holy heavens, and from the throne of Your glory send her, so that being present with me she may labor, and I may know what is well-pleasing before You.
verses.9:11: For she knows and comprehends all things, and she will guide me prudently in my actions and guard me in her glory.
verses.9:12: And my works will be acceptable, and I will judge Your people righteously, and I will be worthy of my father's throne.
verses.9:13: For what man will know the counsel of God? Or who will conceive what the Lord wills?
verses.9:14: For the reasonings of mortals are timid, and our designs are precarious;
verses.9:15: for a perishable body weighs down a soul, and the earthy tent presses down a mind full of many cares.
verses.9:16: And we scarcely surmise the things on earth, and the things at hand we find with labor; but who has traced out the things in the heavens?
verses.9:17: And who has known Your counsel, unless You gave wisdom and sent Your Holy Spirit from on high?
verses.9:18: And in this way the paths of those on earth were set straight, and people were taught the things pleasing to You, and by wisdom they were saved."
verses.10:1: She protected the first-formed father of the world when he was created alone, and she delivered him from his own transgression,
verses.10:2: and gave him strength to rule over all things.
verses.10:3: But when an unrighteous man departed from her in his wrath, he perished together with his brother-killing fury.
verses.10:4: Because of him, wisdom again saved the flooded earth, steering the righteous man by means of humble wood.
verses.10:5: She also, when the nations were thrown into confusion in unanimity of wickedness, found the righteous man, and preserved him blameless before God, and kept him strong in the face of compassion for his child.
verses.10:6: She rescued a righteous man while the ungodly were perishing, as he fled the fire descending on Pentapolis,
verses.10:7: of whose wickedness a smoking wasteland still stands as a testimony, and plants bearing fruit in untimely seasons, and a standing pillar of salt, a monument of an unbelieving soul.
verses.10:8: For by passing by wisdom, they were not only harmed so as not to know what is good, but also left to human life a memorial of their folly, so that in the things in which they stumbled they might not even be able to go unnoticed.
verses.10:9: But wisdom rescued those who served her from hardships.
verses.10:10: She guided a righteous man, a fugitive from his brother's wrath, on straight paths; she showed him the kingdom of God, and gave him knowledge of holy things; she prospered him in his toils, and multiplied the fruits of his labors.
verses.10:11: In the greed of those who overpowered him she stood by him, and made him rich.
verses.10:12: She protected him from enemies, and kept him safe from those lying in ambush; and she decided a fierce contest in his favor, so that he might know that godliness is more powerful than everything.
verses.10:13: She did not abandon a righteous man when he was sold, but rescued him from sin.
verses.10:14: She went down with him into the pit, and in chains she did not leave him, until she brought him the scepter of a kingdom and authority over those who tyrannized him; she also showed those who had found fault with him to be liars, and gave him eternal glory.
verses.10:15: She rescued a devout people and blameless offspring from a nation of oppressors.
verses.10:16: She entered into the soul of a servant of the Lord, and withstood fearsome kings with wonders and signs.
verses.10:17: She repaid the devout the wages of their labors; she guided them on a marvelous way, and became for them a shelter by day and a flame of stars through the night.
verses.10:18: She brought them across the Red Sea, and led them through much water;
verses.10:19: but their enemies she engulfed, and cast them up from the depth of the abyss.
verses.10:20: Therefore the righteous plundered the ungodly, and sang hymns to Your holy name, Lord, and praised with one accord Your defending hand,
verses.10:21: because wisdom opened the mouth of the mute, and made the tongues of infants articulate.
verses.11:1: She prospered their works by the hand of a holy prophet.
verses.11:2: They journeyed through an uninhabited wilderness, and pitched tents in trackless places.
verses.11:3: They withstood foes, and repelled enemies.
verses.11:4: They grew thirsty and called upon You, and water was given to them out of flinty rock, and a remedy for thirst out of hard stone.
verses.11:5: For through the things by which their enemies were punished, through these they themselves were benefited in their need.
verses.11:6: Whereas, instead of the spring of an ever-flowing river, the others were troubled with defiled blood
verses.11:7: as a rebuke for the infant-killing decree, You gave them abundant water unexpectedly,
verses.11:8: showing through the thirst at that time how You punished the adversaries.
verses.11:9: For when they were tested, although disciplined in mercy, they came to know how the ungodly, judged in wrath, were tormented.
verses.11:10: For these You tested like a father who admonishes, but those You examined like a stern king who condemns.
verses.11:11: And both when absent and when present, they were equally distressed.
verses.11:12: For a double grief seized them, and a groaning over memories of the past.
verses.11:13: For when they heard that through their own punishments the others were being benefited, they perceived the Lord.
verses.11:14: For the one who long ago was cast out in exposure they rejected with mockery; at the end of events they marveled at him, having thirsted unlike the righteous.
verses.11:15: And in return for the senseless reasonings of their unrighteousness, in which they went astray and worshiped irrational reptiles and worthless creatures, You sent upon them a multitude of irrational animals for vengeance,
verses.11:16: so that they might know that through the things by which a person sins, through these he is punished.
verses.11:17: For Your all-powerful hand, which created the world out of formless matter, was not at a loss to send upon them a multitude of bears or fierce lions,
verses.11:18: or newly created, unknown wild beasts full of fury, either blowing out fiery breath, or scattering roaring blasts of smoke, or flashing terrible sparks from their eyes—
verses.11:19: beasts whose harm could not only utterly crush them, but whose very sight could terrify and destroy them.
verses.11:20: And even apart from these, they could have fallen by a single breath, pursued by justice and scattered by the breath of Your power; but You set all things in order by measure and number and weight.
verses.11:21: For to have great strength is always present with You, and who will withstand the might of Your arm?
verses.11:22: Because the whole world before You is like a tipping of the balance scales, and like a drop of morning dew that has come down upon the earth.
verses.11:23: Yet You have mercy on all, because You are able to do all things, and You overlook the sins of people for repentance.
verses.11:24: For You love all existing things, and You detest nothing of what You made; for You would not have fashioned anything if You hated it.
verses.11:25: And how would anything have remained if You had not willed it, or that which was not called by You have been preserved?
verses.11:26: Yet You spare all things, because they are Yours, Master, lover of life.
verses.12:1: For Your imperishable Spirit is in all things.
verses.12:2: Therefore, little by little, You reprove those who stumble, and admonish them by reminding them of the things in which they sin, so that, being freed from wickedness, they may believe in You, Lord.
verses.12:3: For indeed, the ancient inhabitants of Your holy land,
verses.12:4: whom You hated for practicing most detestable works of sorcery and unholy rites,
verses.12:5: merciless murderers of children, and a banquet of entrail-eaters of human flesh and blood, initiates from the midst of a cultic revel,
verses.12:6: and parents who murdered helpless souls, You willed to destroy by the hands of our fathers,
verses.12:7: so that the land most precious of all to You might receive a worthy colony of God's children.
verses.12:8: Yet even these You spared as human beings, and You sent wasps as forerunners of Your army, so that they might exterminate them little by little;
verses.12:9: not that You were unable in pitched battle to give the ungodly into the hands of the righteous, or to wipe them out all at once with fierce wild beasts or with a stern word;
verses.12:10: but judging them little by little, You gave a place for repentance, not unaware that their origin was evil and their wickedness inborn, and that their way of thinking would never be changed for all eternity,
verses.12:11: for they were a cursed seed from the beginning; nor was it out of fear of anyone that You granted immunity for the things in which they sinned.
verses.12:12: For who will say, "What have You done?" Or who will resist Your judgment? And who will accuse You for nations that have perished, which You made? Or who will come to confront You as an avenger for unrighteous people?
verses.12:13: For neither is there any god besides You, whose care is for all things, so that You should show that You did not judge unrighteously;
verses.12:14: nor will a king or a tyrant be able to look You in the face concerning those whom You punished.
verses.12:15: But being righteous, You order all things righteously, considering it alien to Your power to condemn the very one who does not deserve to be punished.
verses.12:16: For Your strength is the beginning of righteousness, and Your being Master of all makes You spare all.
verses.12:17: For You display strength when You are disbelieved concerning the perfection of Your power, and among those who know, You rebuke insolence.
verses.12:18: But You, being Master of strength, judge with gentleness, and with great forbearance You govern us; for power is present with You whenever You wish.
verses.12:19: And You taught Your people through such works that the righteous person must be humane; and You made Your sons full of good hope, because You give repentance for sins.
verses.12:20: For if You punished the enemies of Your children, who were also deserving of death, with such great attention and entreaty, giving them times and a place through which they might be freed from wickedness,
verses.12:21: with what great exactness did You judge Your sons, to whose fathers You gave oaths and covenants of good promises?
verses.12:22: Therefore, while disciplining us, You scourge our enemies ten-thousandfold, so that when we judge we may ponder Your goodness, and when we are judged we may expect mercy.
verses.12:23: For this reason also, through their own abominations, You tormented the unrighteous who lived in folly of life.
verses.12:24: For indeed they went farther astray than the ways of error, supposing to be gods those creatures that even among animals are despised by their enemies, being deceived like foolish infants.
verses.12:25: Because of this, as to unreasoning children, You sent judgment as a mockery;
verses.12:26: but those who were not admonished by mocking rebukes will experience a judgment worthy of God.
verses.12:27: For regarding those things at which they themselves were indignant while suffering, being punished by these very ones whom they thought to be gods, they saw and recognized as the true God Him whom they had formerly refused to know; therefore the culmination of condemnation also came upon them.
verses.13:1: For all people were foolish by nature in whom there was ignorance of God, and from the good things that are seen they were unable to know Him who is, nor by paying attention to the works did they recognize the Craftsman.
verses.13:2: Instead, they considered either fire, or wind, or swift air, or the circle of stars, or violent water, or the luminaries of heaven—governors of the world—to be gods.
verses.13:3: And if, delighting in their beauty, they supposed them to be gods, let them know how much better the Master of these is; for the Originator of beauty created them.
verses.13:4: And if they were astounded by their power and activity, let them understand from them how much more powerful is the One who fashioned them.
verses.13:5: For from the greatness of beauty and of created things, their Maker is correspondingly perceived.
verses.13:6: Yet nevertheless, for these there is little blame, for indeed they themselves perhaps go astray while seeking God and wishing to find Him.
verses.13:7: For living among His works, they search diligently, and they are persuaded by sight, because the things that are seen are beautiful.
verses.13:8: Yet again, not even they are excusable;
verses.13:9: for if they were able to know so much that they could investigate the world, how did they not sooner find the Master of these things?
verses.13:10: But miserable are they, and their hopes are in dead things, who called the works of human hands gods: gold and silver, a product of craft, and likenesses of animals, or a useless stone, the work of an ancient hand.
verses.13:11: And even if some woodcutting carpenter, having sawn down a tree easy to move, skillfully scraped off all its bark and, crafting it neatly, fashioned a useful vessel for the service of life,
verses.13:12: and, having used up the scraps of his work for the preparation of food, ate his fill;
verses.13:13: then, taking a scrap from among them that was useful for nothing—a crooked piece of wood grown full of knots—he carved it in the diligence of his idleness and shaped it with the skill of relaxation; he likened it to the image of a man,
verses.13:14: or made it like some worthless animal, coating it with vermilion and reddening its color with rouge, and coating over every blemish in it;
verses.13:15: and having made for it a dwelling worthy of it, he set it in a wall, securing it with iron.
verses.13:16: Therefore, in order that it would not fall down, he provided for it, knowing that it is unable to help itself; for indeed it is an image and has need of help.
verses.13:17: Yet when praying about his possessions and marriage and children, he is not ashamed to speak to the lifeless thing.
verses.13:18: And for health he calls upon what is weak; for life he begs what is dead; for aid he pleads with what is most inexperienced; for a journey, with what is not even able to take a step;
verses.13:19: and for gain and work and success of his hands, he asks capability from what is most incapable in its hands.
verses.14:1: Again, someone preparing for a voyage and about to pass through wild waves calls upon a piece of wood more decayed than the ship carrying him.
verses.14:2: For a desire for gain devised that ship, and wisdom as craftswoman constructed it;
verses.14:3: but Your providence, Father, steers it, because You gave a way even in the sea and a safe path among the waves,
verses.14:4: showing that You are able to save from everything, so that someone may embark even without skill.
verses.14:5: Yet You desire that the works of Your wisdom not be idle; therefore people entrust their lives even to the smallest piece of wood, and passing through the surge on a raft, they are brought safely through.
verses.14:6: For in the beginning also, when the arrogant giants were perishing, the hope of the world took refuge on a raft and, steered by Your hand, left to the age a seed of generation.
verses.14:7: For blessed is the wood through which righteousness comes;
verses.14:8: but what is made by hands is accursed, both it and the one who made it, because the one fashioned it, while the perishable thing was named a god.
verses.14:9: For equally hateful to God are both the ungodly one and his ungodliness;
verses.14:10: for indeed what was done will be punished together with the one who did it.
verses.14:11: Therefore there will also be a visitation upon the idols of the nations, because in God's creation they became an abomination, and stumbling blocks for the souls of people, and a trap for the feet of the foolish.
verses.14:12: For the beginning of sexual immorality is the devising of idols, and their inventions are the corruption of life.
verses.14:13: For neither did they exist from the beginning, nor will they exist forever;
verses.14:14: for by the vainglory of people they entered into the world, and therefore a swift end was devised for them.
verses.14:15: For a father worn down by untimely grief, having made an image of the child quickly taken away, now honored as a god the one who was then a dead human being, and handed down mysteries and rites to those under his authority;
verses.14:16: then in time the ungodly custom, having grown strong, was kept as a law,
verses.14:17: and by commands of tyrants carved images were worshiped. Unable to honor them face to face because they lived far away, people pictured the appearance from afar and made a visible image of the honored king, so that through their zeal they might flatter the absent one as though present.
verses.14:18: And the ambition of the craftsman urged even those who were ignorant to an intensification of worship.
verses.14:19: For he, perhaps wishing to please the ruler, forced the likeness by his skill toward greater beauty;
verses.14:20: and the multitude, drawn in by the charm of the workmanship, now regarded as an object of worship the man who a little while before had been honored.
verses.14:21: And this became a snare for life, because people, enslaved either to misfortune or to tyranny, bestowed the incommunicable name upon stones and wood.
verses.14:22: Then it was not enough for them to go astray concerning the knowledge of God, but living also in a great war of ignorance, they call such great evils peace.
verses.14:23: For celebrating either child-murdering rites, or secret mysteries, or frenzied revelries of strange ordinances,
verses.14:24: they no longer keep either their lives or their marriages pure, but one either kills another by lying in wait, or grieves him by adultery.
verses.14:25: And all things are mixed together indiscriminately: blood and murder, theft and deceit, corruption, faithlessness, tumult, perjury,
verses.14:26: disturbance of the good, forgetfulness of favor, defilement of souls, reversal of generation, disorder of marriages, adultery and debauchery.
verses.14:27: For the worship of nameless idols is the beginning and cause and end of every evil;
verses.14:28: for either while rejoicing they go mad, or they prophesy falsehoods, or they live unjustly, or they quickly commit perjury;
verses.14:29: for trusting in lifeless idols, having sworn wickedly, they do not expect to be harmed.
verses.14:30: Yet both just penalties will overtake them, because they thought wrongly about God by paying heed to idols, and they swore unjustly in deceit, having despised holiness.
verses.14:31: For it is not the power of the things sworn by, but the penalty for those who sin that always pursues the transgression of the unjust.
verses.15:1: But You, our God, are kind and true, patient and governing all things with mercy.
verses.15:2: For even if we sin, we are Yours, knowing Your might; we will not sin, knowing that we are counted as Yours.
verses.15:3: For to know You is complete righteousness, and to know Your might is the root of immortality.
verses.15:4: For neither has the wickedly skilled devising of people led us astray, nor the fruitless labor of painters, a form stained with varied colors,
verses.15:5: the sight of which turns to reproach for the foolish, and one longs for the breathless form of a dead image.
verses.15:6: Lovers of evil things, and worthy of such hopes, are those who make them, and those who long for them, and those who worship them.
verses.15:7: For a potter also, pressing soft earth, laboriously molds each article for our service; yet out of the same clay he molds both the vessels serving clean uses and the opposite ones, all alike; and what the use is of each one of either kind of these, the clay-worker is the judge;
verses.15:8: and in wicked toil he molds a futile god out of the same clay, he who a little while ago came into being from earth and after a little while goes back to that from which he was taken, when the debt of his soul is demanded back.
verses.15:9: Yet his concern is not that he is about to fall ill, nor that he has a brief life, but he rivals goldsmiths and silversmiths, and imitates bronze-molders, and considers it a glory that he molds counterfeits.
verses.15:10: His heart is ashes, and his hope is of less worth than earth, and his life is of less honor than clay,
verses.15:11: because he was ignorant of the One who molded him, and the One who breathed into him an active soul and blew into him a vital spirit;
verses.15:12: but he regarded our life as a game and our living as a profitable festival, for he says one must make gain from any source, even from evil.
verses.15:13: For this man knows above all others that he is sinning, crafting fragile vessels and carved images out of earthy material.
verses.15:14: Yet most foolish and more wretched than the soul of an infant are all the enemies of Your people who oppressed them,
verses.15:15: because they even regarded all the idols of the nations as gods, which have neither the use of eyes for seeing, nor nostrils for drawing in air, nor ears to hear, nor fingers on their hands for feeling, and their feet are useless for walking.
verses.15:16: For a human being made them, and one who has borrowed his spirit molded them; for no human being is able to mold a god like himself;
verses.15:17: yet being mortal, he produces a dead thing with lawless hands; for he is better than the objects of his worship, since he himself lived, whereas they never did.
verses.15:18: And they even worship the most hateful animals; for when compared in senselessness, they are worse than the others.
verses.15:19: Nor are they beautiful enough to be desired, even as far as the appearance of animals goes, but they have escaped both the praise of God and His blessing.
verses.16:1: Therefore they were deservedly punished by similar things, and were tormented by a multitude of vermin.
verses.16:2: Instead of this punishment, showing kindness to Your people, You prepared quail as food, an unusual taste for the desire of appetite,
verses.16:3: so that the former, desiring food, might turn away even from necessary appetite because of the sight shown of the things sent against them, while the latter, having been in want for a little while, might even share in an unusual taste.
verses.16:4: For it was necessary that relentless want should come upon those who were acting as tyrants, while to these it should only be shown how their enemies were being tormented.
verses.16:5: For even when the terrible fury of wild beasts came upon them, and they were perishing by the bites of twisting serpents, Your wrath did not remain to the end;
verses.16:6: but for admonition they were troubled for a little while, having a symbol of salvation as a reminder of the commandment of Your law.
verses.16:7: For the one who turned was not saved because of what was looked at, but because of You, the Savior of all.
verses.16:8: And in this also You convinced our enemies that You are the One who delivers from every evil.
verses.16:9: For the bites of locusts and flies killed them, and no healing was found for their life, because they deserved to be punished by such creatures;
verses.16:10: but not even the teeth of venomous serpents conquered Your sons, for Your mercy came to their aid and healed them.
verses.16:11: For they were stung as a reminder of Your oracles, and were swiftly rescued, so that, falling into deep forgetfulness, they might not become unresponsive to Your kindness.
verses.16:12: For indeed, neither herb nor poultice cured them, but Your word, Lord, which heals all things.
verses.16:13: For You have authority over life and death, and You bring down to the gates of Hades and bring up.
verses.16:14: But a man, though he kills by his wickedness, does not bring back a spirit that has departed, nor release a soul that has been taken.
verses.16:15: Yet it is impossible to escape Your hand.
verses.16:16: For the ungodly, refusing to know You, were scourged by the strength of Your arm, pursued by unusual rains and hailstorms and relentless downpours, and consumed by fire.
verses.16:17: For most astonishing of all, in the water that quenches all things, the fire was all the more active; for the world is a defender of the righteous.
verses.16:18: For at one time the flame was tamed, so that it might not burn up the animals sent against the ungodly, but that they themselves, seeing it, might know that they were being driven by God's judgment;
verses.16:19: and at another time, even in the midst of water, it burns beyond the power of fire, so that it may destroy the produce of an unrighteous land.
verses.16:20: Instead of these things, You fed Your people the food of angels, and sent them prepared bread from heaven without toil, capable of every delight and suited to every taste.
verses.16:21: For Your sustenance manifested Your sweetness toward children; and serving the desire of the one who ate, it transformed itself into whatever anyone wished.
verses.16:22: And snow and ice endured fire and did not melt, so that they might know that fire, burning in the hail and flashing in the rains, was destroying the enemies' crops;
verses.16:23: yet this fire again, so that the righteous might be nourished, has even forgotten its own power.
verses.16:24: For creation, serving You who made it, intensifies for punishment against the unrighteous, and relaxes into kindness on behalf of those who trust in You.
verses.16:25: Therefore at that time also, transformed into all things, it served Your all-nourishing gift, according to the wish of those in need,
verses.16:26: so that Your sons, whom You loved, Lord, might learn that it is not the production of crops that nourishes a person, but Your word preserves those who believe in You.
verses.16:27: For what was not destroyed by fire melted when merely warmed by a brief ray of the sun,
verses.16:28: so that it would be known that one must be ahead of the sun for thanksgiving to You, and at the rising of the light pray to You.
verses.16:29: For the hope of an ungrateful person will melt like winter frost, and will flow away like useless water.
verses.17:1: For great are Your judgments and hard to explain; therefore uninstructed souls went astray.
verses.17:2: For lawless men, supposing that they were oppressing a holy nation, lay as prisoners of darkness and fettered captives of a long night, shut in under roofs, exiles from eternal providence.
verses.17:3: For thinking that they were hidden in secret sins, they were scattered under a dark veil of forgetfulness, dreadfully terrified and deeply troubled by apparitions;
verses.17:4: for not even the recess that held them guarded them free from fear, but deeply troubling sounds resounded around them, and gloomy specters with unsmiling faces appeared.
verses.17:5: And no force of fire was strong enough to give light, nor did the brilliant flames of the stars endure to illuminate that grim night.
verses.17:6: But only a self-kindled blaze full of fear shone through to them, and terrified by that unseen sight, they considered the things they saw to be even worse.
verses.17:7: And the tricks of the magical craft lay prostrate, and there was a humiliating refutation of boasting in understanding.
verses.17:8: For those who promised to drive away terrors and troubles from a sick soul—these were sick with a laughable timidity.
verses.17:9: For even if nothing disturbing frightened them, panicked by the passing of vermin and the hissing of reptiles,
verses.17:10: they were perishing, trembling and refusing to look upon the air that cannot be escaped on any side.
verses.17:11: For wickedness, being condemned, testifies on its own that it is a cowardly thing, and pressed hard by conscience, it has always added distressing things.
verses.17:12: For fear is nothing except a surrender of the aids from reason;
verses.17:13: and expectation, being weaker from within, counts ignorance greater than the cause that produces the torment.
verses.17:14: But they, sleeping the same sleep throughout that truly powerless night, which came out of the recesses of powerless Hades,
verses.17:15: were partly driven by monstrous phantoms and partly paralyzed by the surrender of the soul; for a sudden and unexpected fear came upon them.
verses.17:16: So then, whoever fell down there was kept under guard, shut in the prison without iron.
verses.17:17: For whether someone was a farmer or a shepherd or a laborer at wilderness toils, overtaken, he endured the inescapable necessity.
verses.17:18: For with one chain of darkness they were all bound. Whether a whistling wind, or a melodious sound of birds among spreading branches, or the rhythm of water flowing with force, or the harsh crash of rocks hurled down,
verses.17:19: or the unseen running of leaping animals, or the voice of the most savage roaring wild beasts, or an echo rebounding from the hollow of the mountains—these terrified and paralyzed them.
verses.17:20: For the whole world was illuminated with bright light, and was engaged in unhindered works;
verses.18:1: But for Your devout ones there was a very great light. Hearing their voice yet not seeing their form, they counted them blessed because indeed they too had suffered,
verses.18:2: and because, though previously wronged, they did not harm them, they gave thanks and begged pardon for having been at variance.
verses.18:3: In place of these things, You provided a pillar blazing with fire, as a guide for an unknown journey and a harmless sun for an honorable sojourn.
verses.18:4: For those people deserved to be deprived of light and imprisoned in darkness, who had kept Your sons locked up, through whom the imperishable light of the law was about to be given to the world.
verses.18:5: When they had planned to kill the infants of the devout ones, and one child was exposed and saved, as a reproof You took away the multitude of their children and destroyed them all together in violent water.
verses.18:6: That night was made known beforehand to our fathers, so that, knowing with certainty the oaths they had trusted, they might take heart.
verses.18:7: The salvation of the righteous and the destruction of the enemies were awaited by Your people.
verses.18:8: For as You punished the adversaries, by this You called us to Yourself and glorified us.
verses.18:9: For in secret the devout children of good men were offering sacrifice, and in harmony they established the divine law that the holy ones would share alike in the same good things and dangers, while the fathers were already singing praises beforehand.
verses.18:10: But the discordant cry of the enemies echoed back, and a pitiable cry was carried abroad for the children being lamented.
verses.18:11: And with like penalty a slave was punished together with a master, and a commoner suffered the same things as a king;
verses.18:12: and all of them together, under one name of death, had innumerable dead; for the living were not even sufficient to bury them, since in a single moment their most honored offspring was destroyed.
verses.18:13: For though disbelieving everything because of their sorceries, at the destruction of the firstborn they confessed the people to be God's son.
verses.18:14: For while quiet silence encompassed all things, and night in its own swiftness was in the midst of all things,
verses.18:15: Your all-powerful word leaped from the heavens, from royal thrones, a stern warrior into the midst of the doomed land, carrying Your unfeigned command as a sharp sword,
verses.18:16: and taking its stand, filled all things with death; it touched heaven, yet stood upon the earth.
verses.18:17: Then immediately visions of dreams dreadfully agitated them, and unexpected terrors came upon them,
verses.18:18: and cast down half-dead, one here and another there, each declared the reason why he was dying.
verses.18:19: For the dreams that troubled them had disclosed this beforehand, so that they might not perish without knowing why they were suffering evil.
verses.18:20: Now a trial of death touched the righteous as well, and a plague came upon a multitude in the wilderness; yet the wrath did not remain for long.
verses.18:21: For a blameless man hurried to fight as their champion, bringing the weapon of his own ministry, prayer and the atonement of incense; he withstood the fury and put an end to the calamity, showing that he was Your servant.
verses.18:22: He conquered the crowd not by strength of body, not by the power of weapons, but by word he subdued the punisher, recalling the oaths and covenants of the fathers.
verses.18:23: For when the dead had already fallen in heaps upon one another, he stood between them, drove back the wrath, and severed the path toward the living.
verses.18:24: For upon his full-length robe was the whole world, and the glories of the fathers were upon the four-rowed engraving of stones, and Your majesty was upon the diadem of his head.
verses.18:25: To these the destroyer yielded, and these they feared; for the trial of wrath alone was sufficient.
verses.19:1: But upon the ungodly merciless fury came until the end; for He knew beforehand even their future,
verses.19:2: that after they themselves had relented so as to let them depart and had sent them off with haste, they would change their minds and pursue them.
verses.19:3: For while still having their mourning in hand and lamenting at the tombs of the dead, they drew upon themselves another thought of folly, and those whom they had driven out with entreaties, these they pursued as fugitives.
verses.19:4: For the deserved necessity was dragging them to this end and implanted forgetfulness of what had happened, so that they might fill up the punishment still lacking to their torments,
verses.19:5: and that Your people might experience an extraordinary journey, while those others might find a strange death.
verses.19:6: For the whole creation in its own kind was fashioned anew from the beginning, serving its own commands, so that Your children might be kept unharmed.
verses.19:7: The cloud overshadowing the camp was seen, and out of water that stood before, the emergence of dry land; out of the Red Sea, an unobstructed road, and a grass-bearing plain out of a violent surge,
verses.19:8: through which those who were sheltered by Your hand passed as a whole nation, seeing marvelous wonders.
verses.19:9: For they grazed like horses and leaped about like lambs, praising You, Lord, who delivered them;
verses.19:10: for they still remembered the events of their sojourn, how instead of the birth of living creatures the earth brought forth gnats, and instead of aquatic creatures the river disgorged a multitude of frogs.
verses.19:11: And afterward they also saw a new birth of birds, when, led on by craving, they asked for foods of luxury;
verses.19:12: for as a comfort, quail came up to them from the sea.
verses.19:13: And the punishments came upon the sinners not without the signs that had occurred through the force of the thunderbolts; for they were suffering justly for their own wicked deeds, since they indeed practiced a more grievous hatred of strangers.
verses.19:14: For the former did not receive those unacquainted with them when they arrived, whereas these enslaved guests who were benefactors.
verses.19:15: And not only that, but surely there will be some visitation of them, since they received foreigners with hostility;
verses.19:16: whereas these, after welcoming them with festivities, afflicted with dreadful hardships those who had already shared in the same rights.
verses.19:17: And they too were struck with blindness, just like those at the doors of the righteous man, when, enveloped in yawning darkness, each one sought the passage through his own doors.
verses.19:18: For the elements changed harmony among themselves, just as on a harp the notes alter the name of the rhythm while always remaining constant in tone, which one can infer accurately from the sight of what took place.
verses.19:19: For land creatures were changed into aquatic creatures, and swimming creatures passed over onto land;
verses.19:20: fire in water surpassed its own power, and water forgot its quenching power.
verses.19:21: Conversely, flames did not waste away the flesh of perishable living creatures walking about in them, nor the melting, easily melted ice-like kind of immortal food.
verses.19:22: For in every way, Lord, You magnified Your people and glorified them, and You did not overlook them, standing beside them at every time and in every place.

notes.1:5: Greek elenchthesetai literally means 'will be put to shame' or 'will be rebuked,' here conveying the sense of being offended or repulsed at the approach of unrighteousness.
notes.1:6: Greek ton nephron literally means 'of his kidneys,' a biblical idiom for the seat of one's deepest thoughts, emotions, and conscience.
notes.1:14: Greek hai geneseis literally means 'the generations' or 'things brought into being,' often understood here as 'the creatures' or 'the generative forces.'
notes.1:16: The masculine pronouns ('him,' 'his') refer back to personified Death (v. 13; cf. Hades, v. 14). Greek etakesan ('pined away') literally means 'melted' or 'wasted away.'
notes.2:7: The Greek text reads aeros ('of the air,' attested in major early uncial manuscripts); other witnesses and emendations read earos ('of spring').
notes.2:13: Greek paida can mean either 'child' (connecting with vv. 16 and 18) or 'servant' (echoing Isaiah 52:13 LXX).
notes.2:19: The Greek text reads dikasomen ('judge'), as in Codices Vaticanus and Sinaiticus; other witnesses read dokimasomen ('test' or 'prove').
notes.2:22: The Greek text reads autou ('of Him,' referring to God), continuing 'the mysteries' from the end of v. 21; many manuscripts read theou ('of God').
notes.2:23: The Greek text reads idiotetos ('proper nature' or 'character'); a notable variant reads aidiotetos ('eternity').
notes.3:9: Following Codices Vaticanus and Sinaiticus, the Greek text ends with 'His chosen ones,' omitting the additional clause 'and He watches over His holy ones' found in some witnesses.
notes.3:10: Greek tou dikaiou can be taken either as masculine ('the righteous one,' cf. 2:12) or as neuter ('what is right').
notes.3:14: The opening predicate 'blessed is' is implied from v. 13, and 'a more pleasing lot in the temple of the Lord' alludes to the promise to the eunuch in Isaiah 56:4-5.
notes.3:18: Greek diagnoseos ('decision') is a legal term referring to judicial examination and verdict.
notes.4:6: Greek reads literally "from lawless sleeps," a poetic euphemism for illicit sexual unions.
notes.4:12: Greek uses vivid, rare imagery: "fascination" (baskania) denotes a bewitching spell, "roving" (rhembasmos) restless wandering, and "undermines" (metalleuei) literally means "mines under" (also sometimes taken as "alters" or "perverts").
notes.4:14: The verb "hastened" (espeusen) has no explicit object in Greek; it may be taken intransitively of the righteous person ("he hastened") or, as in the Latin Vulgate, with the Lord as subject ("He hastened [to remove him]").
notes.4:15: The Greek constructs this verse with participles and no finite main verb (an anacoluthon), rendered with finite verbs here for clarity.
notes.5:7: Greek reads eneplēsthēmen ("we were filled / had our fill"); some translators emend the text to eneplakēmen ("we were entangled").
notes.5:14: Greek reads pachnē ("frost"), matching the major uncial witnesses; other manuscripts or conjectures read achnē ("spray" or "chaff") or arachnē ("spiderweb").
notes.5:16: Greek basileion can mean either "royal crown" (parallel here with "diadem") or "kingdom."
notes.5:23: The Greek critical text reads nominative pasa ... anomia ("all lawlessness") as the subject rather than accusative pasan tēn gēn ("the whole earth") found in some other witnesses.
notes.6:9: Greek tyrannoi in this context is a neutral Hellenistic title meaning "monarchs" or "sovereigns" (also in 6:21), not the modern pejorative "tyrants."
notes.6:10: The Greek uses a threefold wordplay on the same root: hosiōs ta hosia hosiōthēsontai ("who keep holy things in holiness will be made holy").
notes.6:12: The Saints Greek Critical Text follows the shorter uncial reading and does not include the additional clause "and is found by those who seek her" present in some other witnesses.
notes.7:2: "Ten-month period" reflects the ancient reckoning of human gestation by ten lunar months; "congealed in blood" echoes ancient embryological imagery (cf. Job 10:10).
notes.7:3: Greek homoiopathē (lit. "of like nature/experiences") applied to the earth either points to the earth's shared nature with earthborn humanity (7:1) or acts as a transferred epithet for the common mortal lot of all born onto it.
notes.7:12: Following the critical Greek reading genesin ("origin" or "source"); some later witnesses and versions read genetin ("mother" or "begetter").
notes.7:20: Greek pneumatōn can mean either "winds" (fitting the natural-philosophy catalog) or "spirits" (reflecting Hellenistic Jewish traditions of Solomon's knowledge over spiritual forces).
notes.7:26: Greek apaugasma can denote either active "radiance/effulgence" shining forth from light or passive "reflection" (cf. Hebrews 1:3).
notes.8:4: Greek mystis ("initiate") borrows from Hellenistic mystery terminology to portray wisdom as one initiated into the inner secrets of God's knowledge.
notes.8:7: The four virtues listed here—self-control (sōphrosynē), understanding/prudence (phronēsis), righteousness/justice (dikaiosynē), and courage (andreia)—are the classical Greek cardinal virtues.
notes.8:20: Scholars debate whether "being good, I entered an undefiled body" reflects a Hellenistic/Platonic view of the preexistence of the soul or is a rhetorical self-correction locating personal identity in the soul rather than the body.
notes.8:21: Greek enkratēs appears without an explicit object and can mean either "in possession [of wisdom]" (fitting 8:18 and 9:4, 17) or "self-controlled/continent" (as rendered in the Latin Vulgate).
notes.9:1: Following the critical Greek text reading tou eleous sou ("of Your mercy"); some Greek witnesses omit sou ("Lord of mercy").
notes.9:4: Greek thronōn (lit. "thrones," also in 9:12) is a poetic plural referring to a single royal throne (cf. singular thronou in 9:10); Greek paidōn can mean either "children" or "servants."
notes.9:15: The imagery of a perishable body and "earthy tent" (skēnos) weighing down the soul echoes Hellenistic philosophical language and parallels the tent metaphor of 2 Corinthians 5:1–4.
notes.10:3: Greek synapoleto (lit. 'perished together with') indicates that the unrighteous man (Cain) brought about his own ruin along with his fratricidal fury.
notes.10:6: Pentapolis (lit. 'Five Cities') is the Greek name for the five cities of the plain—Sodom, Gomorrah, Admah, Zeboiim, and Zoar (cf. Gen 14:2; 19:24-26).
notes.10:10: 'Holy things' translates an ambiguous Greek plural (hagion) that can also mean 'holy ones' (i.e., angels, alluding to Jacob's vision at Bethel in Gen 28:12). 'The fruits of his labors' renders tous ponous autou (lit. 'his labors'), a Septuagint idiom for the yield or earnings of work.
notes.10:12: Greek ebrabeusen uses athletic umpire imagery ('decided the contest in his favor' or 'awarded the prize'), alluding to Jacob's wrestling match at the Jabbok (Gen 32:24-30).
notes.11:6: The Greek text reads the masculine plural participle tarachthentes ('having been troubled'), a syntactic shift (anacoluthon) referring to the enemies of v. 5 in contrast to 'them' (Israel) in v. 7. Other manuscripts read the singular genitive tarachthentos ('of a river fouled with defiled blood').
notes.11:14: Alludes to the infant exposure of Moses (Exod 2:3). The Greek text reads the finite verb apeipon ('they rejected') rather than a participle.
notes.11:17: 'Out of formless matter' (ex amorphou hyles) employs Hellenistic philosophical vocabulary to describe the primordial state of creation in Gen 1:2.
notes.11:18: Greek bromous ('roars' or 'roaring blasts') is spelled with omicron here; some interpreters take it as an alternate spelling of bromos with omega ('foul fumes/stench').
notes.11:26: Greek philopsyche (lit. 'lover of soul/life') reclaims a classical term normally meaning 'clinging to one's own life' to express God's loving care for all living beings.
notes.12:5: The Greek syntax is compressed and textually debated: the accusative singular noun "banquet" (thoinan) is coordinated directly with personal nouns ("murderers," "initiates"), and the genitive plural splanchnophagon ("of entrail-eaters") appears where some manuscripts read the accusative singular splanchnophagon ("an entrail-eating banquet").
notes.12:12: The preposition kata with the genitive carries a Hellenistic legal sense of "concerning" or "for" in both clauses, and katastasis denotes a formal appearance or confrontation in court.
notes.12:20: Translates the Greek text deeseos ("entreaty" or "supplication"); some critical editions adopt the conjecture dieseos ("leniency" or "indulgence").
notes.12:24: The phrase ta kai en zoois ton echthron atima ("those creatures that even among animals are despised by their enemies") is difficult; ton echthron may also be taken as neuter ("of hateful creatures"), and some editions conjecture aischron ("vile").
notes.13:5: Follows the Greek word order megethous kallones kai ktismaton ("the greatness of beauty and of created things"); other witnesses place the conjunction earlier to read "the greatness and beauty of created things."
notes.13:9: Greek stochasasthai ton aiona literally means "to conjecture" or "to investigate the world" (or "age"), referring to cosmological speculation and calculation.
notes.13:11: The vignette opens with a conditional ei de kai ("And even if") that unfolds through verses 11-15 with aorist verbs in a loose grammatical construction (anacoluthon) characteristic of vivid Hellenistic diatribe.
notes.13:13: Translates the Greek reading aneseos ("relaxation" or "leisure"), paralleling "idleness" (argias) in the previous clause; some manuscripts read syneseos ("understanding" or "skill").
notes.14:12: Greek porneia encompasses both literal sexual immorality (developed in vv. 24-26) and the biblical metaphor of idolatry as spiritual unfaithfulness. The Greek text here reads the plural heureseis ('inventions').
notes.14:21: Greek akoinoneton ('incommunicable') literally means 'not to be shared with any other,' referring to God's exclusive divine name.
notes.14:24: Greek notheuon ('by adultery') literally means 'corrupting' or 'making illegitimate,' referring to marital betrayal that undermines a household's lineage.
notes.14:26: Greek geneseos enallage ('reversal of generation') is debated, understood either as unnatural sexual inversion or as confusion of birth and lineage through adultery.
notes.14:27: Greek anonymon ('nameless') can also carry the sense 'unmentionable' or 'not to be named' (cf. Exod 23:13 LXX), contrasting with God's 'incommunicable name' in v. 21.
notes.15:4: Greek skiagraphon ('painters') literally refers to 'shadow-painters,' artists who used shading and perspective to create lifelike illusions.
notes.15:5: Following the Greek manuscript reading oneidos ('reproach') rather than the conjectural emendation orexin ('desire,' reflected in the Vulgate). The abrupt shift from plural 'the foolish' to the singular verb pothei ('one longs for') is a known syntactic difficulty in the Greek text.
notes.15:9: Greek kamnein ('fall ill') can mean 'grow weary,' 'fail in strength,' or 'fall ill,' pointing here to the potter's approaching frailty and mortality.
notes.15:17: The Greek connecting relative hon (lit. 'of which') is syntactically compressed, functioning here in a causal or contrastive sense ('since he himself lived, whereas they never did').
notes.16:3: The Greek text reads ten deichtheisan ('the [sight] shown'), a feminine participle without an expressed noun (perhaps implying 'sight' or 'appearance'). Many critics emend or adopt the reading eidechtheian ('loathsomeness' or 'hideousness').
notes.16:10: The verb antiparelthen literally means 'came forward to meet' or 'intervened to help,' used positively here of God's rescuing mercy (contrast its sense 'passed by on the other side' in Luke 10:31-32).
notes.16:11: The adjective aperispastoi ordinarily means 'undistracted,' but here with the genitive it carries the sense 'unmoved by,' 'unresponsive to,' or 'cut off from' God's kindness.
notes.16:21: Greek hypostasis can mean either 'sustenance/provision' (referring to the manna) or 'substance/nature' (referring to God's own essence revealed in the gift).
notes.16:25: The verb metalleuo ordinarily means 'to mine,' but the author of Wisdom uses it (here and in 4:12) to mean 'to alter' or 'to transform,' apparently playing on meta ('change') and allos ('other').
notes.17:6: The genitive phrase 'that unseen sight' is syntactically debated: it can be taken as causal with 'terrified' ('terrified by that unseen sight') or as comparative with 'worse' ('worse than that unseen sight').
notes.17:11: The Greek text reads idios ... martyrei ('testifies on its own') and proseilephen ('has added/taken on'), where some witnesses or critics read idio martyri ('condemned by its own witness') and proeilephen ('has anticipated/forecast').
notes.17:13: This compressed philosophical sentence is notoriously difficult: 'expectation' (prosdokia) likely refers to expectation of aid from v. 11, and 'the cause' may be construed either as comparative ('greater than the cause') or as objective with 'ignorance' ('ignorance of the cause').
notes.18:1: The Greek text translated here reads 'hoti men oun kakeinoi epepontheisan' (without a negative particle, as in the major uncials). Other witnesses and ancient versions read 'ou' ('not') instead of or with 'oun', yielding 'because those others had not also suffered'.
notes.18:9: This text reads the genitive absolute 'paterōn ēdē proanamelpontōn ainous' ('while the fathers were already singing praises beforehand'); other witnesses read nominative 'proanamelpontes' ('already singing the praises of the fathers').
notes.18:14: The Greek text repeats 'ta panta' ('all things') after 'mesazousēs' ('was in the midst of all things'), whereas some witnesses omit the repeated phrase ('was midway [in its course]').
notes.18:22: The principal manuscripts read 'ton ochlon' ('the crowd'); many commentators emend this by letter transposition to 'ton cholon' ('the wrath/anger').
notes.18:25: The major manuscripts shift abruptly from singular 'ho olothreuōn' ('the destroyer') to plural 'ephobēthēsan' ('they feared'); some witnesses smooth this to singular 'ephobēthē' ('he feared').
notes.19:2: The Greek text reads 'epistrepsantes tou apeinai' ('having relented/turned around so that they might be gone'), attested in major uncials; other witnesses and editions read 'epitrepsantes tou apienai' ('having permitted them to depart').
notes.19:6: This text reads 'tais idiais epitagais' ('its own commands', following Vaticanus and Sinaiticus), whereas other witnesses read 'tais sais epitagais' ('Your commands').
notes.19:15: The text reads 'all' ē tis episkopē estai autōn' ('but surely there will be some visitation of them'). Because uncial script had no spaces or accents ('ALLĒTIS'), many editors read 'all' ei tis' ('but if there will be some allowance/regard for them').
notes.19:18: The author compares the miraculous interchange of the four elements to harp notes shifting the character ('name') of a rhythm while keeping their pitch; the neuter participle 'menonta' ('remaining constant') agrees grammatically with 'ta stoicheia' ('the elements').
notes.19:21: The Greek text has the double adjective 'tēkton eutēkton' ('melting, easily melted', as in Vaticanus), which many editors regard as an early scribal corruption of 'etēkon eutēkton' ('nor did they melt the easily melted...').

unplaced.text: but over those alone a heavy night was spread, an image of the darkness that was about to receive them; yet to themselves they were heavier than darkness.
unplaced.note: The verb form epetato is best understood as a shortened spelling or haplography for epetetato ('was stretched/spread over,' from epiteino), governing the dative 'over those alone.' This verse has no separate place in the Saints.Bible numbering, so it is shown after 17:20.
